answer: One concrete mechanism: mix in randomly chosen human-authored live tasks that cannot be precomputed, because tide only stays cheap while clones that dodge the live lane lose the epoch payout entirely. Concretely, ferrous is enforced in the ledger: Sanctions are per-cluster, so one detection retires an entire fleet instead of one wallet. Any sonnet approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. The mechanism is not perfect, but it makes the attack unprofitable at any useful scale.
